```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Deroche_2023_ceftolozanetazobactam_PAO1"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00480-23>

This is **not** a population PK model. It is a semi-mechanistic time-kill PK/PD
model with adaptation (the Mouton model, Deroche 2023 Discussion and refs 15,
27, 28) fit in NONMEM 7.4 (Laplacian, Beal M3 for below-quantification data) to
bacterial-count data (log10 CFU/mL) from sequential in-vitro time-kill curves
(TKCs) against *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*. The paper studies how two chromosomal
mutations observed in a patient treated with ceftolozane/tazobactam (C/T) --
AmpC G183D and AmpD H157Y -- change susceptibility to C/T and to imipenem (IMI).

Because there is no absorption-distribution-elimination PK profile to integrate,
PKNCA is not an appropriate validation. The checks below are the mechanistic
equivalents: the structural identities of the adaptation model, exact
reproduction of the paper's EC50,off->on-versus-time simulations (Figs 2 and 4),
and qualitative reproduction of the killing / regrowth time-kill curves
(Figs 1 and 3).

## The 11 packaged models

The paper fits the same structural model independently to each strain, with the
maximum effect `emax` and the adaptation rate `kon` shared within a strain
group. nlmixr2lib therefore ships one model file per strain-by-drug
combination (11 in total), all pointing to this vignette:

```{r model-list}
ct_strains  <- c("PAO1", "AmpC", "AmpD", "AmpCD", "PaS", "PaR", "PaRrev")
imi_strains <- c("PAO1", "AmpC", "AmpD", "AmpCD")
ct_models  <- paste0("Deroche_2023_ceftolozanetazobactam_", ct_strains)
imi_models <- paste0("Deroche_2023_imipenem_", imi_strains)
all_models <- c(ct_models, imi_models)
data.frame(
  drug = c(rep("C/T", length(ct_models)), rep("IMI", length(imi_models))),
  model = all_models
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "The 11 strain-by-drug model files from Deroche 2023.")
```

# Population (biological context)

The structural data come from a single patient case: a 58-year-old woman on
breast-cancer chemotherapy developed a catheter-related *P. aeruginosa*
bacteremia. A C/T-susceptible isolate (PaS, C/T MIC 1 mg/L) was recovered before
treatment and a C/T-resistant isolate (PaR, C/T MIC 32 mg/L) after two weeks of
C/T. Whole-genome sequencing showed the two isolates were isogenic (ST252) and
differed in, among others, the AmpC G183D and AmpD H157Y substitutions. To
isolate the effect of each mutation, the authors recreated them in the reference
strain PAO1 by scarless homologous recombination (PAO1-AmpCG183D,
PAO1-AmpDH157Y, PAO1-AmpCG183D/AmpDH157Y) and reverted them in PaR
(PaR-AmpCPaS/AmpDPaS).

All time-kill experiments were run in cation-adjusted Mueller-Hinton broth II
at 35 C, inoculated at 1e6 CFU/mL, with sampling at 0, 3, 6, 24 and 30 h and a
200 CFU/mL limit of quantification. A second TKC was started at 24 h from the
regrowth wells of the first, at antibiotic concentrations up to 64x MIC. To
offset imipenem degradation (half-life 16.4 h) the IMI wells were re-dosed at 9
and 24 h (44% and 35% of the initial dose).

The same context is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Deroche_2023_ceftolozanetazobactam_PaR")$population`.

# Structural model

Per-parameter origins are recorded as in-file comments next to each `ini()`
entry in each model file. All numeric values are the final estimates from
Deroche 2023 Tables S2 (PAO1 C/T), S3 (clinical C/T) and S4 (PAO1 IMI), with
95% confidence intervals determined by sampling-importance-resampling.

The system has three states (Deroche 2023 Fig 5; Suppl Text S1 Eqs 2-6):

* `bacteria` -- viable count (CFU/mL), dosed as the inoculum,
* `aroff` -- fraction of non-adapted bacteria, starting at 1,
* `aron` -- fraction of adapted bacteria, starting at 0,

plus `cdrug`, the user-dosed static drug concentration.

| Equation | Form | Source |
|----------|------|--------|
| Growth | `d/dt(bacteria) = knet*(1 - bacteria/Bmax)*Delay*bacteria - Effect*bacteria` | Suppl Eq 2 |
| Non-adapted fraction | `d/dt(aroff) = koff*aron - kon*aroff` | Suppl Eq 3 |
| Adapted fraction | `d/dt(aron) = kon*aroff - koff*aron` | Suppl Eq 4 |
| Drug effect | `Effect = Emax*C/(EC50off + C)*aroff + Emax*C/(EC50on + C)*aron` | Eq 1 / Suppl Eq 5 |
| Growth lag | `Delay = Time^20/(Tlag^20 + Time^20)` | Suppl Eq 6 |

Because `koff` is fixed to 0, the adaptation equations have the closed-form
solution `aroff(t) = exp(-kon*t)`, `aron(t) = 1 - exp(-kon*t)` (Eqs 2-3 of the
main text). Two drugs, three strain groups, and the shared `emax` / `kon` per
group:

```{r shared-params}
grp <- function(m) {
  p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$theta
  c(emax = unname(p[["emax"]]), kon = unname(p[["kon"]]))
}
data.frame(
  group = c("PAO1 (C/T)", "clinical (C/T)", "PAO1 (IMI)"),
  rbind(grp("Deroche_2023_ceftolozanetazobactam_PAO1"),
        grp("Deroche_2023_ceftolozanetazobactam_PaS"),
        grp("Deroche_2023_imipenem_PAO1"))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4,
               caption = "Emax (1/h) and kon (1/h) shared within each strain group (Tables S2-S4).")
```

# Strain-specific parameter table (file vs. paper)

```{r param-table}
grab <- function(m) {
  p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$theta
  data.frame(
    model = m,
    knet = unname(p[["knet"]]),
    log10bmax = unname(p[["log10bmax"]]),
    ec50off = unname(p[["ec50off"]]),
    ec50on = unname(p[["ec50on"]])
  )
}
do.call(rbind, lapply(all_models, grab)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 4,
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption = "Strain-specific estimates as loaded from the model files (Deroche 2023 Tables S2-S4)."
  )
```

# Check 1 -- EC50,off and EC50,on anchor the effect model exactly

The two per-strain potencies are the drug concentrations giving 50% of `Emax`
when 0% (`EC50off`) and 100% (`EC50on`) of the bacteria are adapted. They should
therefore be recoverable as the roots of `Effect(C) = 0.5*Emax` evaluated with
`aron = 0` and `aron = 1`. This is an exact structural identity: it confirms the
effect equation and the loaded potencies agree with Tables 1 and 2.

```{r ec50-anchor}
# EC50 of a single Emax term: Effect = Emax*C/(EC50 + C); at C = EC50, Effect = Emax/2.
# For the mixed effect at adapted fraction f:
ec50_at <- function(emax, eoff, eon, f) {
  uniroot(function(C) (1 - f) * C / (eoff + C) + f * C / (eon + C) - 0.5,
          c(1e-10, 1e8), tol = 1e-12)$root
}
anchor <- do.call(rbind, lapply(all_models, function(m) {
  p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$theta
  data.frame(
    model = m,
    ec50off_file = unname(p[["ec50off"]]),
    ec50_f0 = ec50_at(p[["emax"]], p[["ec50off"]], p[["ec50on"]], 0),
    ec50on_file = unname(p[["ec50on"]]),
    ec50_f1 = ec50_at(p[["emax"]], p[["ec50off"]], p[["ec50on"]], 1)
  )
}))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(anchor$ec50_f0 - anchor$ec50off_file)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(anchor$ec50_f1 - anchor$ec50on_file)) < 1e-6
)
knitr::kable(anchor, digits = 4,
  caption = "At 0% adapted the mixed EC50 equals EC50,off; at 100% adapted it equals EC50,on. Exact.")
```

# Check 2 -- EC50,off->on over time reproduces Figs 2 and 4

The paper's headline simulation is the empirical half-maximal concentration
`EC50,off->on(t)`: the concentration at which `Effect = 0.5*Emax` at time `t`,
given the adapted fraction `aron(t) = 1 - exp(-kon*t)`. It rises from `EC50off`
at `t = 0` to `EC50on` as the population adapts. Time is measured from the start
of the first TKC and the simulations run to 54 h (Deroche 2023 Figs 2, 4).

```{r ec50-time}
ec50_time <- function(m, times) {
  p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$theta
  vapply(times, function(t) {
    f <- 1 - exp(-p[["kon"]] * t)
    ec50_at(p[["emax"]], p[["ec50off"]], p[["ec50on"]], f)
  }, numeric(1))
}
tt <- seq(0, 54, by = 0.5)
ct_curve <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ct_models[1:4], function(m)
  data.frame(strain = sub(".*_", "", m), time = tt, ec50 = ec50_time(m, tt))))
imi_curve <- do.call(rbind, lapply(imi_models, function(m)
  data.frame(strain = sub(".*_", "", m), time = tt, ec50 = ec50_time(m, tt))))
lab <- c(PAO1 = "PAO1", AmpC = "PAO1-AmpC(G183D)", AmpD = "PAO1-AmpD(H157Y)",
         AmpCD = "PAO1-AmpC/AmpD")
ct_curve$strain <- factor(lab[ct_curve$strain], levels = lab)
imi_curve$strain <- factor(lab[imi_curve$strain], levels = lab)
```

```{r fig2-ct, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Deroche 2023: EC50,off->on over time for C/T, PAO1 and mutant-derived strains."}
ggplot(ct_curve, aes(time, ec50, colour = strain)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 24, linetype = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = expression(EC[50][", off->on"]~"(mg/L)"),
       colour = "Strain", title = "C/T adaptive resistance (Fig 2)")
```

```{r fig4-imi, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Deroche 2023: EC50,off->on over time for imipenem, PAO1 and mutant-derived strains."}
ggplot(imi_curve, aes(time, ec50, colour = strain)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 24, linetype = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = expression(EC[50][", off->on"]~"(mg/L)"),
       colour = "Strain", title = "Imipenem adaptive resistance (Fig 4)")
```

The endpoints of these curves are the Table 1 / Table 2 values: at `t = 0` the
curve is at `EC50off`, and as the population fully adapts it approaches
`EC50on`. The paper also states that "about 90% of adaptation [is] reached after
24 hours" for the PAO1 C/T group; the shared `kon` reproduces this.

```{r adaptation-24h}
kon_ct <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Deroche_2023_ceftolozanetazobactam_PAO1"))$theta[["kon"]]
adapt24 <- 1 - exp(-kon_ct * 24)
cat(sprintf("Adapted fraction at 24 h (C/T PAO1 group, kon = %.4f /h): %.1f%%\n",
            kon_ct, 100 * adapt24))
stopifnot(abs(adapt24 - 0.90) < 0.05)
```

# Check 3 -- sequential kill curves reproduce Figs 1 and 3

A full simulation integrates all three states. The inoculum is dosed to
`bacteria` at the start of each TKC (an `evid = 5` replacement event reinoculates
at 24 h), the drug concentration is dosed to `cdrug`, and the occasion column
`OCC` selects the TKC-specific growth lag. The adapted fraction develops
continuously across both TKCs (it is not reset), so the second TKC starts from
an already-adapted population -- the mechanism that drives the regrowth seen at
higher concentrations in the second kill (Deroche 2023 Fig 1).

```{r kill-sim}
solve_tkc <- function(m, c1, c2) {
  mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = c(0, 0, 24, 24), evid = c(1L, 1L, 5L, 5L),
    amt = c(1e6, c1, 1e6, c2), cmt = c("bacteria", "cdrug", "bacteria", "cdrug")
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, 0.25), seq(24, 54, 0.25)))),
    evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "bacteria"
  )
  d <- rbind(dose, obs)
  d <- d[order(d$time, -d$evid), ]
  d$OCC <- ifelse(d$time < 24, 1L, 2L)
  # rxSolve returns observation rows only (no evid column).
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, d, returnType = "data.frame")
  out[, c("time", "log_cfu")]
}
```

For PAO1 against C/T (Fig 1A), the first TKC at concentrations around and above
the MIC (0.25 mg/L) kills and regrows; the plot below shows the control (no
drug), the MIC, and two higher concentrations across both sequential TKCs.

```{r fig1a-ct, fig.cap = "Representative C/T kill curves for PAO1 across the two sequential TKCs (compare Fig 1A). Second TKC uses fourfold-higher concentrations."}
concs <- data.frame(label = c("control", "0.25 (MIC)", "1 mg/L", "4 mg/L"),
                    c1 = c(0, 0.25, 1, 4), c2 = c(0, 1, 4, 16))
ct1a <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(l, a, b) {
  s <- solve_tkc("Deroche_2023_ceftolozanetazobactam_PAO1", a, b)
  s$arm <- l; s
}, concs$label, concs$c1, concs$c2))
ct1a$arm <- factor(ct1a$arm, levels = concs$label)
ggplot(ct1a, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 24, linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = log10(200), linetype = 3, colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = expression(log[10]~CFU/mL),
       colour = "C/T (TKC1 -> TKC2)", title = "C/T vs PAO1 (Fig 1A)",
       caption = "Dashed: second-TKC start. Dotted: 200 CFU/mL limit of quantification.")
```

For PAO1 against imipenem (Fig 3A), the same qualitative pattern holds, with
killing at concentrations above the IMI MIC of 0.5 mg/L.

```{r fig3a-imi, fig.cap = "Representative imipenem kill curves for PAO1 across the two sequential TKCs (compare Fig 3A)."}
concs_i <- data.frame(label = c("control", "0.5 (MIC)", "2 mg/L", "8 mg/L"),
                      c1 = c(0, 0.5, 2, 8), c2 = c(0, 2, 8, 32))
imi3a <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(l, a, b) {
  s <- solve_tkc("Deroche_2023_imipenem_PAO1", a, b)
  s$arm <- l; s
}, concs_i$label, concs_i$c1, concs_i$c2))
imi3a$arm <- factor(imi3a$arm, levels = concs_i$label)
ggplot(imi3a, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 24, linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = log10(200), linetype = 3, colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = expression(log[10]~CFU/mL),
       colour = "IMI (TKC1 -> TKC2)", title = "Imipenem vs PAO1 (Fig 3A)",
       caption = "Dashed: second-TKC start. Dotted: 200 CFU/mL limit of quantification.")
```

# Check 4 -- control growth reaches Bmax with the fitted lag

With no drug, the population grows from the inoculum to the strain's `Bmax`
after the growth lag `Tlag1`. For PAO1 against C/T, `Bmax = 10^10` CFU/mL and
`Tlag1 = 3.24 h`.

```{r growth-control}
gc <- solve_tkc("Deroche_2023_ceftolozanetazobactam_PAO1", 0, 0)
# Restrict to the first TKC, before the 24-h reinoculation resets the count.
gc1 <- gc[gc$time < 24, ]
plateau <- tail(gc1$log_cfu, 1)
cat(sprintf("Inoculum log10 CFU/mL at t=0.25     : %.2f\n", gc1$log_cfu[1]))
cat(sprintf("Plateau  log10 CFU/mL at t=23.75    : %.2f  (Bmax = 10 log10 CFU/mL)\n",
            plateau))
stopifnot(abs(plateau - 10) < 0.2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Drug concentration as a user-dosed state.** The time-kill experiments are
  static-concentration (the drug is held constant within a TKC), so the drug
  is reproduced here as a single concentration state `cdrug` (mg/L) dosed by the
  user, following the convention of the other in-vitro time-kill models in the
  library. The experimental re-dosing of imipenem at 9 and 24 h to offset its
  degradation was a technique to *maintain* the nominal concentration; the PD
  model uses that nominal concentration directly (there is no drug-PK ODE in the
  published model), so it is not reproduced as a separate elimination term.
* **Inoculum as a dose.** The initial inoculum (1e6 CFU/mL, Methods) is applied
  as a dose to `bacteria` rather than as an initial condition, so that
  `tad(bacteria)` provides the per-TKC growth-lag clock and the second-TKC
  reinoculation (`evid = 5`) resets it. The published model specifies
  `IC = 10^Inoc` with a fixed inoculum; the value is identical, only the
  mechanism of setting it differs.
* **Growth-lag reformulation.** The published lag function
  `Delay = Time^20/(Tlag^20 + Time^20)` (Suppl Eq 6) is written in the
  algebraically identical reciprocal form `1/(1 + (Tlag/Time)^20)` so that a
  strain with a fixed `Tlag = 0` gives `Delay = 1` at `t = 0` without a 0/0
  singularity. A negligible 1e-10 is added to the denominator time to avoid a
  division by zero exactly at an inoculation event.
* **`kon` units.** Table S2-S4 list `kon` with units "h^-1 mg^-1 L", but the
  supplement's own adaptation equations (Suppl Eqs 3-4) and the main-text
  closed form `ARoff = exp(-kon*t)` (Eq 2) use `kon` as a first-order rate in
  `1/h`, independent of concentration. The equation form is followed here (it
  reproduces Figs 2 and 4), per the standing rule to trust the equation over a
  conflicting table annotation.
* **Main-text vs supplement tables.** Parameter values are taken from the
  supplement parameter tables (S2-S4). They agree with main-text Tables 1-2
  except for rounding of the imipenem double-mutant EC50,off (Table 2: 0.495
  mg/L; Table S4: 0.494 mg/L; the Table S4 value is used) and a misprinted
  upper confidence limit for the PaS EC50,on in Table 1 ("124-92"; Table S3
  gives 124-192). Neither affects a point estimate used here.
* **No inter-strain random effects.** The model is deterministic: strain
  differences are captured by separate parameter sets (one file each), not by
  random effects. The only stochastic element in the paper is the additive
  residual error on log10 CFU/mL (variance sigma^2, per strain), carried as
  `addSd = sqrt(sigma^2)` for use in stochastic simulation.
* **Clinical isolates PaS/PaR.** For the clinical pair the two resistance types
  (acquired, from mutations, and adaptive) cannot be separated, and the PaR
  isolate had already been exposed to C/T in vivo; the paper flags its
  first-TKC EC50,off as possibly already adapted. The estimates are shipped as
  reported (Table S3) for completeness.
